hook.line: Vale is writing the new menu and gets stuck on the very first drink. *agua* is a *la* word, so why does everyone say *el agua*?
hook.es: Prefiero el agua fría, por favor.

examples.es: El área de la cocina es pequeña.

rule:
*agua* is a *la* word, but *la agua* would run two a's together right where your voice leans on the word. So Spanish swaps in *el*, and *un* for *una*:
*el agua*, *un agua*, *el hambre*, *el área*

That's the only change. The word is still feminine, so everything else stays feminine:
*el agua fría*, *mucha hambre*, *el área es pequeña*, *esta agua*

In the plural the problem disappears: *las aguas*.

The swap only happens when the a- at the start is the loud part of the word. *arepa* leans on *re*, so it keeps *la arepa*.
smallPrint: Teachers say *el* goes before feminine nouns that start with a stressed *a-* (a tónica).

pitfalls.why: Almost. The *el* is only for the sound; *agua* is still feminine, so *fría*.
Before a stressed a-, Spanish says *el*: *el agua*.
